chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, or I heard him say:

If a man forgets a phrase from the adhān until he begins the iqāmah, then let him proceed with the iqāmah, and there is nothing upon him. But if he forgets a phrase from the iqāmah, he returns to the phrase that he forgot.
Then he says: “From that place to the end of the iqāmah.”

And regarding a man who forgets to separate between the adhān and the iqāmah by something until he starts the salat (prayer) or gives the iqāmah for the salat, he said: “There is nothing upon him, but he is not allowed to leave that deliberately.”
Then he was asked: What suffices of tasbīḥ between the adhān and the iqāmah? He said: “He says: al-ḥamdu lillāh.”

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the second call announcing the immediate start of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: the phrase 'All praise belongs to Allah'
key_terms.حَرْفًا: a phrase or wording unit omitted in recitation
key_terms.يَفْصِلَ: to make a separation or interval

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets part of the adhān or iqāmah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings related to forgetting parts of the adhān or iqāmah and the recommended separation between them. If part of the adhān is forgotten after beginning the iqāmah, one continues, but if part of the iqāmah is forgotten, one returns to the missed phrase and continues from there. It also states that a minimal dhikr between the adhān and iqāmah can be saying "al-ḥamdu lillāh."
